appliesTo.versions: reported with 3.5.3 (Spring Boot 3.5.5, Hibernate 6.6.26); worked with Spring Boot 3.3.5; issue milestone 3.4.10 (2024.1.10)

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Repository creation fails during application startup because an @Query string containing /* ... */ block comments is rejected with BadJpqlGrammarException ('mismatched input /'). The same code started fine on Spring Boot 3.3.5.
cause: Spring Data JPA's own HQL query parser (HqlParser, ANTLR-based, in the stack trace) did not accept block comments, so parsing stops at the first '/'.
fixSummary: A contributed change to the Spring Data JPA query parsers to accept comments was taken up by the maintainer (who also asked for the same handling in the EQL and JPQL parsers); the issue is tracked against milestone 3.4.10 (2024.1.10), so upgrade to a maintenance release containing it.
notes: Interim workaround of removing the comments from the @Query text is an inference, not stated in the thread. Fix details (merged PR) are inferred from the closed state, milestone and the maintainer's reply.

	at com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonGenerator._constructWriteException(JsonGenerator.java:2937)
	at com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonGenerator._reportError(JsonGenerator.java:2921)
	at com.fasterxml.jackson.core.json.UTF8JsonGenerator.writeFieldName(UTF8JsonGenerator.java:217)
	at org.springframework.batch.core.repository.dao.Jackson2ExecutionContextStringSerializer$JobParametersModule$JobParameterSerializer.serialize(Jackson2ExecutionContextStringSerializer.java:213)

appliesTo.versions: 6.0.1 with the deprecated Jackson2ExecutionContextStringSerializer kept after upgrading from 5.2.x; issue milestone 6.0.2

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: After upgrading from Spring Batch 5.2.3 to 6.0.1 while keeping Jackson2ExecutionContextStringSerializer, running a job that contains a JobStep fails when the step execution context is persisted, with JsonMappingException/JsonGenerationException 'Can not write a field name, expecting a value' on the JobParameters set.
cause: The JobParameter serializer inside the deprecated Jackson 2 execution-context serializer wrote a field name where a value was expected for the Spring Batch 6 job parameter model; a maintainer reproduced the failure with a nested-job (JobStep) sample.
fixSummary: Fixed in 6.0.2 by a commit that changes how the job parameter is written. Maintainers recommend migrating to the Jackson 3 based JacksonExecutionContextStringSerializer on v6; the fix was not backported to 5.2.x because JobParameter in v5 does not carry its name.
notes: Exact content of the fix for the Jackson 2 serializer is inferred from a commenter's remark and the maintainer's backport explanation. Maintainers also state that serialized contexts are not compatible between 5.x/Jackson 2 and 6.x/Jackson 3, so jobs started on v5 should be completed on v5.

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Test cleanup that calls JobRepositoryTestUtils.removeJobExecutions(list) on JobExecution objects from earlier launches fails with OptimisticLockingFailureException 'Attempt to delete step execution ... with wrong version', where it worked on 5.2.2.
cause: Since 5.2.3 (change tracked as #4793 in the project) deleting step executions checks the entity version, and the JobExecution instances kept by the test hold stale versions after the job ran.
fixSummary: Workaround from a contributor: re-query each JobExecution from the job repository to get its latest version before deleting. A maintainer planned a library fix in 6.0.2, backported to 5.2.5.
notes: Fix versions are the maintainer's stated plan at the time the issue was closed.

errorSample:
Caused by: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.exc.InvalidDefinitionException: Direct self-reference leading to cycle (through reference chain: riskop.MyIllegalArgumentException["cause"])
        at com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.exc.InvalidDefinitionException.from(InvalidDefinitionException.java:77)
        at com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.SerializerProvider.reportBadDefinition(SerializerProvider.java:1359)
        at com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ser.BeanPropertyWriter._handleSelfReference(BeanPropertyWriter.java:953)
        at com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ser.BeanPropertyWriter.serializeAsField(BeanPropertyWriter.java:726)
        at com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ser.std.BeanSerializerBase.serializeFields(BeanSerializerBase.java:760)
        at com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ser.std.BeanSerializerBase.serializeWithType(BeanSerializerBase.java:643)
        at com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ser.impl.TypeWrappedSerializer.serialize(TypeWrappedSerializer.java:32)
        at com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ser.DefaultSerializerProvider._serialize(DefaultSerializerProvider.java:503)

appliesTo.versions: 2.19.0 (Spring Boot 3.5.0); fixed in 2.20.0

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: With an ObjectMapper configured as setVisibility(ALL, NONE) plus setVisibility(FIELD, ANY) and default typing, serializing a custom exception class fails with InvalidDefinitionException 'Direct self-reference leading to cycle' on the 'cause' property, while serializing the identical JDK exception works.
cause: Throwable.cause is set to the exception itself to mean 'no cause'; getCause() converts that to null but direct field access does not. With getters disabled and fields auto-detected, Jackson serializes the raw cause field and sees a self-reference.
fixSummary: Fixed on the serialization side in 2.20.0. Config-level workaround confirmed by the reporter: do not disable method auto-detection (drop setVisibility(PropertyAccessor.ALL, Visibility.NONE)), so getCause() is used.
notes: The maintainer noted deserialization might still have separate problems and asked for a follow-up issue if so.

title: Jackson 2.21 throws 'Conflicting property-based creators' when both a no-arg and a multi-arg constructor carry @JsonCreator
errorSample:
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Conflicting property-based creators: already had explicit creator [constructor for `com.example.Main$AllDefaultsJava` (0 args), annotations: {interface com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonCreator=@com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonCreator(mode=DEFAU ...
	at com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.introspect.PotentialCreators.setPropertiesBased(PotentialCreators.java:31)

appliesTo.versions: 2.21.0 through 2.21.2 (worked in 2.20.0); fixed in 2.21.3 and 3.1.1

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Deserializing a class that annotates both its default (0-arg) constructor and a multi-arg constructor with @JsonCreator fails with IllegalArgumentException 'Conflicting property-based creators', although the same code worked in 2.20.0. The reporter sees the same pattern with Kotlin data classes that have default values and @JsonCreator.
cause: Jackson 2.21 added stricter creator-precedence handling and treats the extra @JsonCreator on the no-arg constructor as a conflicting explicit creator. The maintainer called that usage ambiguous but agreed existing users should not break.
fixSummary: The maintainer restored acceptance of this pattern; fixed in the 2.21 branch (released as 2.21.3) and in 3.1.1. Until upgrading, removing the redundant @JsonCreator from the no-arg constructor avoids the conflict (inference from the maintainer's remark that the no-arg annotation is never used).
notes: 2.21.3 had not been released when the issue was closed; the maintainer expected it within about a month.

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Calling authenticationProviders(providers -> providers.clear(); add custom providers) on the authorization endpoint configurer makes application startup fail with IllegalArgumentException 'authenticationValidator cannot be null' from OAuth2AuthorizationCodeRequestValidatingFilter.
cause: OAuth2AuthorizationCodeRequestValidatingFilter, introduced in 7.0.1 to fix an earlier bug, receives its validator composite only through the default OAuth2AuthorizationCodeRequestAuthenticationProvider; when that provider is removed from the list the validator stays null. This reading comes from the reporters' analysis of the configurer; the maintainer confirmed the failure and said the filter was meant as a temporary hidden fix.
fixSummary: A maintainer commit resolved the null failure (issue milestone 7.0.8). The maintainer also planned to expose the validating filter as a public, configurable part of the API in a later release (7.2.0-M2 was targeted) as a separate enhancement.
notes: Keeping the default provider in the list instead of clearing it is a likely workaround but is an inference, not stated in the thread.

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Launching a job with JobLauncher.run fails with DataAccessResourceFailureException 'Hibernate transaction: Unable to commit against JDBC Connection; This connection has been closed' (PSQLException); another user hit 'The object is already closed' on H2 in JdbcJobInstanceDao.getJobInstance.
cause: In 5.2.3 JdbcTemplate.queryForStream was used inside try-with-resources in the JDBC DAOs; closing the stream closes the connection that the surrounding transaction still needs. Commenters traced it to a regression from a stream-based change (PR 4802).

notes: The reporter used Zonky embedded Postgres in tests; the H2 report suggests the problem is not database specific.

title: WebClient request hangs or times out silently when a cookie name contains an invalid character
errorSample:
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Cookie name contains an invalid char: @
		at io.netty.handler.codec.http.cookie.CookieEncoder.validateCookie(CookieEncoder.java:38)
		at io.netty.handler.codec.http.cookie.ClientCookieEncoder.encode(ClientCookieEncoder.java:217)
		at io.netty.handler.codec.http.cookie.ClientCookieEncoder.encode(ClientCookieEncoder.java:165)
		at reactor.netty.http.client.HttpClientOperations.beforeMarkSentHeaders(HttpClientOperations.java:629)

appliesTo.versions: before 1.2.10 (observed through Spring WebClient); fixed in 1.2.10

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: A WebClient request that sets a cookie whose name contains an illegal character such as '@' never completes (or only hits the configured timeout) and no exception reaches the caller; the IllegalArgumentException is visible only in a DEBUG log line 'An outbound error could not be processed'.
cause: Netty's cookie encoder rejects names that are not valid RFC 6265 tokens (for example containing '@'), and Reactor Netty did not propagate that outbound IllegalArgumentException to the subscriber.
fixSummary: Fixed in Reactor Netty 1.2.10 (change referenced by the maintainer) so the error is surfaced. The cookie name itself must still be valid; a commenter noted a raw Cookie header bypasses the validation if a non-compliant name is unavoidable.
notes: The raw-header suggestion comes from a non-maintainer commenter.

appliesTo.versions: 3.5.3 (also main at report time); fixed in 3.5.6, issue milestone also lists 3.4.10

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: On IBM Semeru Runtime for z/OS, launching a Spring Boot executable jar fails in NestedJarFile.getManifestInfo with UncheckedIOException caused by IOException 'invalid header field (line 1)' when the manifest entry is stored (not deflated).
cause: In JarEntryInputStream of NestedJarFile the 'remaining' counter was not initialized for stored entries, so available() returned a wrong value. IBM's alternative Manifest implementation peeks at available() to detect ASCII data and fell back to EBCDIC-1047, producing garbage.
fixSummary: A maintainer fixed the initialization; the reporter confirmed the fix with a 3.5.6 snapshot and it was released with 3.5.6 (18 September 2025 per the maintainer).

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: After ResolvableType.getGenerics() has been called on a generic type, Java-serializing that ResolvableType throws NotSerializableException for sun.reflect.generics.reflectiveObjects.TypeVariableImpl, while serializing it before the call works.
cause: getGenerics() lazily fills a cached field with ResolvableType instances that reference java.lang.reflect.Type implementations such as TypeVariableImpl, which are not Serializable.
fixSummary: The maintainer marked the lazily computed volatile fields as transient (changing the serialized form is acceptable because Spring gives no cross-version serialization guarantee); fixed in 7.0.5 with a backport planned for 6.2.17.

symptom: After upgrading from Gradle 9.4.1 to 9.5.0, a large multi-module build exhausts the daemon heap; the daemon log shows OutOfMemoryError and MessageIOException, and a heap dump shows build-operation queues and compile-related data retained across tasks.
cause: According to the fixing pull request, worker runnables of DefaultBuildOperationQueue were left hanging (waiting for worker leases) instead of being run only when a worker lease was available, so queued operations and the data they reference piled up. appliesTo.versions: 7.0.x after the change to native request header handling (seen with Spring Boot 4.0.3); fixed in 7.0.7

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: A GraphQL-over-WebSocket subscription that reads handshake headers in an interceptor works on Spring Boot 3.5.11 but on 4.0.3 the socket closes with code 1011 and the server logs IllegalStateException: The request object has been recycled and is no longer associated with this facade.
cause: Spring Framework began exposing HTTP request headers directly from the servlet request without copying. WebSocket handshake headers were then read after the handshake exchange completed, when Tomcat had already recycled the request object.
fixSummary: A maintainer confirmed it as a Framework regression and fixed it by copying the handshake header values into the WebSocket session instead of keeping a reference to the original request headers; fixed in 7.0.7.

appliesTo.versions: 6.0.4 (Spring Boot 4.1.0); fixed in 6.1.0-M2

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: On application shutdown the container calls close() on every JpaCursorItemReader bean, including readers whose step never ran, and logs a WARN 'Custom destroy method close ... propagated an exception' with ItemStreamException 'Error while closing item reader' caused by a NullPointerException.

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Building a chunk-oriented step that calls skip(SomeException.class) but not skipLimit() fails at build time with IllegalArgumentException 'The skipLimit must be greater than zero'.
cause: The new ChunkOrientedStepBuilder defaults skipLimit to -1 and builds a LimitCheckingExceptionHierarchySkipPolicy when skippable exceptions are set, whose constructor rejects non-positive limits. The previous fault-tolerant builder defaulted the limit to 10.

symptom: Deserializing a Kotlin class with a @JvmInline Long wrapper from a JsonNode via treeToValue, with the id given as a JSON string needing coercion, fails with DatabindException caused by NullPointerException 'this._readCapabilities is null'. Numeric JSON, or readValue from a String, works.

symptom: When a parameter or schema default value is defined, serving the OpenAPI document fails with InvalidDefinitionException because java.util.Optional is not supported by the mapper, so the UI does not load.

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue; only a short error excerpt is quoted. Original text © its authors.

symptom: Every query on an entity with @Field("itm") on a property named items produces a PropertyReferenceException 'No property itm found for type CaseEntity; Did you mean id, items' from QueryMapper.filterUnwrappedObjects, although the queries still work because the exception is caught internally.
cause: The application's @Query fields projection names the database field ('itm') instead of the mapped property name ('items'), so the mapper cannot resolve a property path for it. The reporter found this while building a reproducer and closed the issue as their own usage problem.
fixSummary: Use property names, not stored field names, in the fields specification of @Query (the reporter's corrected usage); the logged exception is otherwise harmless.
notes: The corrective step is inferred from the reporter's description 'we use field names rather than property names'; the maintainer only confirmed closure.
